fixes.explanation: False. Jesus says nothing about the man joining the Twelve. He says, "Do not stop him…" and then gives His reason: "…no one who performs a miracle in My name can turn around and speak evil of Me." The joining part isn't in the text.

Tongue seems like a natural next one, but Jesus doesn't list it here. He goes from the hand to the foot, and then to the eye. His words are, "And if your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out." Those are the three He names in this passage.

Heart is a good guess, since so much of life starts there. But in this passage Jesus names the hand, then the foot, then the eye. His words are, "And if your eye causes you to sin, pluck it out." The heart isn't one of the three He lists.
Teaching it is. Jesus did not want anyone to know, because He was teaching His disciples. I think of it as a classroom on the move, with a teacher and His students walking through Galilee.
Right. Jesus says the Son of Man will be delivered into the hands of men, and "They will kill Him…" He doesn't dress it up or soften it. I think that is a heavy thing to hear on a walk.
A crown isn't what Jesus says, friend. He says, "They will kill Him…" Those are plain words, and a crown doesn't appear anywhere in that sentence. This is a heavy part, so I'll just say it plainly.
The first half checks out. They did not understand what Jesus said. But the second half doesn't match the text. It says "…they were afraid to ask Him about it." They didn't ask Him to explain.

Yes. They had been arguing about which of them was the greatest. When Jesus asked what they were discussing, they were silent. When a room goes quiet like that, I think they already knew what He'd say.

I see why you'd guess that, since the spirit they couldn't drive out comes just before this (Mark 9:18). But the text never says they argued about it. It says that on the way they had been arguing about which of them was the greatest.
It's actually True. John, one of the disciples, says, "…we tried to stop him…" They didn't just watch the man. They stepped in, and John tells Jesus so himself.
Where the man was from never comes up. John says they tried to stop him because "…he does not accompany us." Galilee isn't given as a reason.
That's the one. Jesus says, "For whoever is not against us is for us." Short line, big door. Anyone who is not against them is for them.
People lose their way in parking garages all the time, so that one's a real thing. But Jesus doesn't say way here. He says the one who gives a cup of water "…will never lose his reward."

True, and I think this one is heavy. Jesus says if anyone causes one of these little ones who believe in Him to stumble, it would be better for him to have a large millstone hung around his neck and be thrown into the sea. Those are His words, with nothing softened.

The kingdom of God. Jesus says it is better "…to enter the kingdom of God with one eye than to have two eyes and be thrown into hell…" That is His warning about an eye that causes you to sin. This is a heavy part, so I'll just say it plainly.

That's it. Jesus says, "Salt is good, but if the salt loses its saltiness, with what will you season it?" He asks it as a question and leaves it there. And then He gives them something to do with salt.
Salt. Jesus says, "Have salt among yourselves…" Just before that, He talks about salt and its saltiness. Then He adds, "…and be at peace with one another."
